chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Mustawrid al-Nakha'i, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, among the angels who are in the sky of the world, there are those who look upon one, two, or three people when they are mentioning the virtues of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them). So they say: 'Do you not see these few in their scarcity and the abundance of their enemies, describing the virtues of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them)?'
So the other group of angels say: 'That is Allah's grace; He grants it to whom He wills, and Allah is the Lord of mighty grace.'

key_terms.سَمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا: the sky of the world (lowest heaven)

ai.seo_question: What do the angels in the sky of the world say about the few who praise the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the spiritual potency of the *Fuqaha* and scholars, illustrating how even small, humble groups can withstand overwhelming opposition through divine grace (*fadl*). It underscores the Shia theological concept that the preservation of religious knowledge and the Ahl al-Bayt's legacy relies not on numerical strength but on God's selective bestowal of favor upon the righteous.

en.hubeali: H 14969 – From him, from Ahmad, from Ali Bin Al-Mustawarad Al-Nakha’ie, from the one who reported it: Abu Abdullahasws has said;

‘From the Angels who are in the sky of the world, they come to one, and two, and three when they are mentioning the virtues of the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, so they say: ‘But did you see those in their scarcity (of numbers) and the abundance of their enemies, describing the virtues of the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>?’
So the other group of Angels say: “[62:4] That is Allah's grace; He grants it to whom He pleases, and Allah is the Lord of mighty grace”.
en.sarwar: 522. From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al-Hakam, from Umar Bin Hanzala, who has reported the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said: ‘O Umar, do not place a burden upon our (a.s.) Shites, and be kind to them, for the people cannot bear what you can bear’.
